case_number: CIVIL APPEAL NO. 14604 OF 2024 (Arising out of SLP (C) No.36440 of 2014) and CIVIL APPEAL NO. 14605 OF 2024 (Arising out of SLP (C) No.1184 of 2015)

parties.petitioner: Rajendra Kumar Barjatya and Another, Rajeev Gupta and Others
parties.respondent: U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad & Ors.

summary: The appellants, owners of commercial shops constructed on a residential plot in Shastri Nagar, Meerut, challenged the Allahabad High Court's order allowing demolition of unauthorized constructions. The High Court had directed demolition by December 31, 2014, criminal proceedings against erring officers, and departmental action for dereliction of duty. The appellants argued long possession, regularization via freehold deed 'as is where is', valid purchases, and violation of natural justice due to lack of notice under Section 82 of the U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad Adhiniyam, 1965. They cited delay, laches, and selective enforcement. The respondent housing board contended the construction was unauthorized on a residential plot, notices were issued to the allottee, and demolition was justified under law. The Supreme Court considered whether the High Court erred in ordering demolition without exploring regularization, and whether principles of natural justice and lawful procedure were followed.
legal_provisions_cited: U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad Adhiniyam, 1965, Sections 82, 92-94 r/w 3, 7, 8
Municipal Corporation, Ludhiana v. Inderjeet Singh (2008) 13 SCC 506
final_judgment: Leave granted; the appeal was allowed in part with directions for reconsideration of regularization and compliance with due process, while upholding the authority's right to enforce lawful development norms.
